messages:
devon: heads-up — just finished running the split A/B on the new v2q-lite variant against prod traffic slice A. quick summary below.

nina: nice, numbers?

devon: overall intent-accuracy is stable (+0.4% ±0.6), but we saw a 2.8x jump in hallucination_rate on long-contexts (docs > 4k tokens). latency_p95 +18ms. token_cost delta -22%.

ash: that hallucination spike on long docs is concerning. which cohort triggered it?

devon: cohort: "longdoc-heavy-rerank" — ~3.6k requests sampled. the drift appears when the model is forced to compress embeddings for context windows > 4096 during quantized KV merge.

jia: can you paste the gating config used for the canary? want to check the thresholds we used.

devon: pasted below:
```json
{
  "canary": {
    "initial_fraction": 0.01,
    "max_fraction": 0.25,
    "promotion_step": 2,
    "slo": {"latency_p95_ms": 220, "error_rate_pct": 0.5},
    "quality_gates": {
      "fidelity_score_delta": -0.8,
      "hallucination_rate_delta_pct": 1.0,
      "variance_multiplier": 2.0
    },
    "auto_fallback": {
      "enabled": true,
      "trigger_window_minutes": 30,
      "consecutive_windows": 2
    }
  }
}
```

nina: looks standard. but our hallucination gate is set to 1.0% delta — the observed jump is +1.7% absolute, which should have tripped fallback. did the rollout reach the threshold?

devon: interesting part: the metric pipeline tags those long-context requests as "cold-kv-warmup" and they were routed through the "low-priority" sample path that doesn't evaluate hallucination_rate in real time (we only compute that offline). so auto_fallback didn't see the signal.

ash: that's bad — metric tagging gap. we should not send un-evaluated slices into a canary with auto_fallback enabled.

jia: proposed quick mitigation: add a rule excluding cohorts where realtime_quality == false from progressive promotion. small config tweak:
```yaml
canary.exclude_cohorts:
  - name: longdoc-heavy-rerank
    realtime_quality: false
```

devon: implemented patch on staging. rolling to canary config now. deploy-bot: apply canary config change to staging and hold existing traffic.

deploy-bot: ack — applying config update to canary-staging-12. will not change traffic weights. :gear:

nina: follow-up Q: for long-term, should we adjust the hallucination gate to be relative (percent uplift) or absolute? we hit +1.7% absolute but relative uplift was large because baseline was low.

ash: prefer a hybrid: require both absolute delta > 0.5% AND relative uplift > 30% of baseline. that avoids false positives on noisy small cohorts.

jia: agree. also add monotonic hysteresis so once gated the model must pass two consecutive windows to promote. the auto_fallback already has consecutive_windows=2 but we need the symmetric promote condition.

devon: capturing design: "cohort-holdfast" — hold traffic for cohorts where either the absolute or relative quality gate trips. hold persists until 2 consecutive windows of healthy metrics. also we add a sentinel realtime metric for hallucination on longdocs (lightweight heuristic) to unblock auto_fallback.

nina: timeline?

devon: sentinel heuristic implemented in telemetry repo, PR up: https://git.internal/r/telemetry/1234 — staging tests green. will gate-prod deploy pending +1 from ops.

ash: +1 from me. ops: want to review the revert playbook?

jia: ops sign-off: verify rollback latency and model pin behavior. fallback behavior should route traffic to v2-stable and mark offender with tag `cohort-holdfast/longdoc`.

deploy-bot: scheduled config rollout window: 02:15 UTC. will run dry-run then apply. will report back.

devon: thanks all. postmortem note: we exposed a pipeline blindspot — never allow canary promotions for cohorts without realtime eval hooks. adding to onboarding checklist. :memo:
